item.title: Irreducible Representations of Groups
item.description: Definition Let a group $G$ and a finite dimensional vector space $V$ be given. Call $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ the general linear group. The following group homomorphism $\rho$ is called a representation of $G$ on $V$. $$ \rho : G \to \operatorname{GL}(V) $$ $\rho$-Invariant A subspace $W$ of $V$ is said to be $\rho$-[invariant] or $G$-invariant if it satisfies the following. $$ \rho (g) (W) \subset W, \qquad \forall g \in G $$

item.title: Lie Groups
item.description: Definition1 A group $G$ is called a Lie group if it satisfies the following conditions: It has a differentiable structure. The binary operation $\cdot : G \times G \to G$ defined in $G$ is differentiable. The inverse ${}^{-1} : G \to G$ is differentiable. Explanation Simply put, a Lie group is a differentiable group.
